The big read

First UFC main event for both men. Fight-day lines are the Friday, Sept. 25 snapshot; all 24 fighters made weight.

Main event · Bantamweight · 5 rounds
Raul Rosas Jr.@raulrosasjr12–1 · age 21 · southpaw
VS
Raoni Barcelos22–5 · age 39 · orthodox
−175 / +150Rosas / Barcelos
5 straightWins for each
18 yearsAge gap

Rosas signed from Contender Series at 17 and has evolved from blitz-submission hunter into a high-volume wrestling grinder. Barcelos arrives at 39 on the best run of his UFC career after decisions over Talbott, Garbrandt, Simon and Jackson.

The hinge: Rosas has never seen round four. Barcelos must survive the younger man’s back-taking pressure, answer in the clinch, and turn the final ten minutes into a veteran’s test.

Guide lean: Rosas by control, with honest caution. Combat Edge’s 66% projection essentially matches the current market, while Barcelos’s +150 still pays for the most important unknown: championship rounds.

25

New territory

Rosas has never fought beyond 15 minutes. Barcelos’s composure is most valuable if this reaches rounds four and five.

2×

TUF finals

Osmanli–Akylbek Uulu and Amaya–Machado settle both Season 34 tournaments on the main card.

5

Market steam

Vieira, Harrell, Jackson, Castaneda and Jauregui all moved toward favorite territory since Monday—important market-disagreement signals, not guarantees.

Four pressure points

The tactical questions most likely to decide Saturday.

Can Rosas own round four?

His pace is the weapon and the uncertainty. Barcelos has spent years surviving exactly the scrambles the favorite wants.

The market reversed two fights

Vieira and Harrell moved from pick’em to −155 and −142. Their opponents Bryczek +133 and Brener +122 remain live dogs if the steam overshot.

Two TUF contracts, two tests

Osmanli’s finishing creativity meets Uulu’s discipline; Amaya’s unbeaten athleticism meets a champion who has never been finished.

Forty-eight-hour replacement

Unbeaten DWCS signing Luis Hernandez debuts at light heavyweight against Sedriques Dumas less than two weeks after earning his contract.

The big read

Five bouts, all scheduled for three rounds. Current prices are Monday snapshots from BoydBets and Verdict MMA; openers from MMAOddsBreaker.

Main event · Middleweight · 3 rounds
Norbert Növényi Jr.@magicnorbi10–1 · London Shootfighters
VS
Theo Haig@theohaig7–1 · AKA · 100% finishes
−450 / +354Növényi / Haig
−800Növényi opener
7 / 7Haig wins by submission

Növényi brings a 6–1 Bellator run, fluid karate-stance striking and three straight first-round finishes. Haig is back after a 36-second loss on Season 9, carrying a credible BJJ threat and very little margin for another defensive mistake.

The hinge: Haig must get to a takedown before Növényi’s speed and timing expose his overextended striking. The underdog is live early; every clean standing minute favors the favorite.

Guide lean: Növényi by strikes. The price is steep, and Haig’s move from +550 to +354 is worth respecting rather than dismissing.

Unbeaten prospects collide

Contracts awarded

Four pressure points

The contract-night questions that matter.

Haig has one clean route

Close distance, finish a takedown and hunt the submission before Növényi’s striking layers take over.

Two perfect records break

Dasuyev–Ortega and Guaylupo–Connor force four unbeaten prospects to reveal how their skills translate under UFC scrutiny.

Champion versus champion

Degli’s LFA finishing streak meets Moran’s Fury FC grit and deeper experience against UFC-level opposition.

The market cannot name the opener

BoydBets leaned Piwowarczyk; Verdict MMA flipped it toward Quissua. Résumé and unbeaten upside are in direct tension.

Underdog value board

UFC Vegas 121 · Fight-day lines ranked by realistic path, matchup and favorite-fade logic—not certainty.

#1
Best five-round price

Raoni Barcelos

+150

Veteran defensive grappling, five straight wins and proven composure attack Rosas’s biggest unknown: rounds four and five. At −175, the favorite’s hype is no longer discounted.

#2
Best minute-winning dog

Norma Dumont

@norma_dumont_mma
+117

Cleaner range striking and veteran pacing can bank minutes if she denies the clinch; Perez’s six-fight streak may overprice one wrestling route.

#3
Best prospect-side dog

Melissa Amaya

@melissa.amaya27
+180

Unbeaten pressure, athleticism and five finishes create a real upset path; Machado’s championship résumé may overstate the gap in a TUF final.

#4
Best scramble swing

Ilimbek Akylbek Uulu

+240

Disciplined top control can mute Osmanli’s submission chaos; the favorite’s spectacular TUF finishes are carrying a premium.

#5
Best rematch leverage

Ricky Simon

@rickysimonufc
+173

He already beat Jackson once and still owns the pressure-wrestling route; Jackson’s move from −170 to −205 may be too steep after two split losses.

Higher-variance dogs: Dumas +205 gets a debutant opponent on 48 hours’ notice, but enters on a three-fight stoppage-loss skid and is fighting for his roster spot. Brener +122 and Bryczek +133 are also live after the market reversed their bouts toward Harrell and Vieira.
